parts.text: What is its mechanism of action?

parts_raw.text: What is its mechanism of action?

questions.model_answer:
a) Remdesivir is an adenosine nucleotide analogue prodrug; it is metabolized intracellularly to the active triphosphate (GS-441524-TP), which competes with ATP for incorporation by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (nsp12) and causes delayed chain termination of nascent viral RNA, evading proofreading by the nsp14 exonuclease.
b) (1) Ebola virus (filoviruses). (2) Nipah virus (paramyxo/henipavirus). It also has in vitro/animal activity against respiratory syncytial virus.

questions.model_answer:
a) (1) Membrane (M). (2) Envelope (E). (3) Nucleocapsid (N).
b) Remdesivir is a monophosphoramidate prodrug of an adenosine nucleoside analogue; it is metabolized intracellularly to the active triphosphate, which competes with ATP for incorporation by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (nsp12) and causes delayed chain termination, stalling viral RNA synthesis. It also evades proofreading by the coronavirus nsp14 exonuclease.
c) (1) MERS-CoV (and SARS-CoV) in mouse and rhesus macaque models. (2) Ebola virus (also Marburg and Nipah viruses in nonhuman primate models).

cohort_answer.text: Proteins: E protein (envelope); M protein (membrane); N protein (nucleocapsid). Remdesivir MOA: It is a prodrug, nucleoside analog, inhibits viral replication by inhibiting RNA dependent RNA polymerase enzyme, inserting itself into RNA product and stalling RNA synthesis. Other viruses: Other coronaviruses (Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus), Ebola, Marburg (Filoviruses)

questions.question: You see an 80-year-old unvaccinated patient with COVID-19. His past medical history is significant for coronary artery disease and atrial fibrillation. His medications include aspirin and rivaroxaban. He is deemed high-risk for progression to severe disease and is being considered for nirmatrelvir/ritonavir.
questions.question_raw: You see an 80 year-old patient with COVID-19 who is unvaccinated. His past medical history is significant for coronary artery disease and atrial fibrillation. His medications include Aspirin and Rivaroxaban. He is deemed high-risk for progression to severe disease and is being considered for Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir.

parts.text: What are the specific mechanisms of action of nirmatrelvir and ritonavir?
In what adult population would the dose of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir need to be adjusted?
The patient is a candidate for nirmatrelvir/ritonavir. What is another consideration based on his medical history?

parts_raw.text: What are the specific mechanisms of action of Nirmatrelvir and Ritonavir?
In what adult population would the does of Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir need to be adjusted?
The patient is a candidate for Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir. What is another consideration based on his medical history?

questions.model_answer:
a) Nirmatrelvir is a peptidomimetic inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro / 3C-like protease, nsp5), blocking cleavage of the pp1a/pp1ab polyproteins into functional non-structural proteins and thereby halting viral replication. Ritonavir has no anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity; it is a pharmacokinetic booster - a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor that slows nirmatrelvir metabolism to maintain therapeutic plasma concentrations.
b) Moderate renal impairment: eGFR 30 to <60 mL/min - reduce to nirmatrelvir 150 mg with ritonavir 100 mg twice daily for 5 days. Not recommended at eGFR <30 mL/min or in severe (Child-Pugh C) hepatic impairment; no adjustment for mild-moderate hepatic impairment or eGFR >=60.
c) Drug-drug interaction: ritonavir's CYP3A4 (and P-gp) inhibition markedly raises rivaroxaban levels, with a high bleeding risk; the combination is contraindicated. Options are to withhold rivaroxaban (generally not acceptable in atrial fibrillation), switch to an alternative anticoagulant strategy such as low-molecular-weight heparin with expert/pharmacy input, or - preferred - give an alternative antiviral such as remdesivir, which has no significant interaction. Full medication review for other CYP3A substrates (e.g. amiodarone, statins, colchicine) is also required.
questions.beyond_mandell: NIH/IDSA COVID-19 treatment guidelines and the Paxlovid product monograph provide the renal dose adjustment and the rivaroxaban contraindication.

questions.model_answer:
a) Nirmatrelvir inhibits the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (3C-like protease, nsp5), preventing polyprotein processing and viral replication. Ritonavir is not an active antiviral here; it is a CYP3A4 inhibitor used as a pharmacokinetic booster to sustain nirmatrelvir concentrations.
b) Patients with moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30 to <60 mL/min) require reduction to 150 mg/100 mg twice daily for 5 days; it is not recommended with eGFR <30 mL/min or in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C).
c) (1) Ritonavir-boosted therapy is contraindicated with rivaroxaban - CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition raises rivaroxaban levels and bleeding risk, compounded by concurrent aspirin. (2) Substitute remdesivir (3-day outpatient course) as the antiviral, or manage anticoagulation with pharmacy input. (3) Screen all his other medications (amiodarone, statins, digoxin, calcium channel blockers) for CYP3A interactions, and counsel on vaccination after recovery and on possible viral rebound.

parts.text: Mechanism of nirmatrelvir and ritonavir.
When to adjust the dose.
What are the considerations in this case of an 80-year-old unvaccinated male with COVID-19, on rivaroxaban and aspirin for atrial fibrillation, for whom nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is being considered?

parts_raw.text: Mechanism of nirmatrelvir and ritonavir
When to adjust dose
Considerations in case of 80 yo male not vaccinated and diagnosed with COVID-19, on Xarelto and ASA for Afib, wanting to give nirmatrelvir/ritonavir - what are considerations in this case

questions.model_answer:
a) Nirmatrelvir: peptidomimetic inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (3CLpro/nsp5), blocking polyprotein cleavage and viral replication. Ritonavir: no independent anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity; a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor that boosts nirmatrelvir plasma levels.
b) eGFR >=60 mL/min: 300/100 mg PO BID x 5 days. eGFR 30 to <60: reduce to 150/100 mg BID x 5 days. eGFR <30 (including dialysis): not recommended in the label; if used off-label, a reduced regimen (300/100 on day 1 then 150/100 daily) has been described. Mild-moderate hepatic impairment: no adjustment; severe (Child-Pugh C): not recommended.
c) (1) Rivaroxaban is a CYP3A4/P-gp substrate - ritonavir boosting substantially increases exposure and bleeding risk; this combination should be avoided, especially with concomitant aspirin. (2) Preferred alternative is remdesivir 200 mg then 100 mg daily x 3 days as outpatient, with no relevant interaction. (3) Review the remainder of his medications for CYP3A interactions (amiodarone commonly used in atrial fibrillation, statins for coronary artery disease), and counsel on vaccination once recovered and on possible symptomatic rebound.
questions.beyond_mandell: Renal dosing thresholds and the rivaroxaban contraindication come from the Paxlovid product monograph and NIH/IDSA COVID-19 guidelines.

cohort_answer.text:
Mechanism: Nirmatrelvir is a peptidomimetic inhibitor of the main protease (3C-like protease/nsp5), preventing processing of polyprotein precursors and inhibiting viral replication. Ritonavir is a booster with no independent antiviral activity that boosts plasma levels of nirmatrelvir.
When to adjust dose: CrCl >60: 300/100mg BID. CrCl 30-60: 150/100mg BID. CrCl <30: not recommended, but risk of harm is low with a 5-day course; can try 300/100 day one then 150/100 daily days 2-5, or 150/100 daily x5 days (well tolerated). Dialysis: 300/100 day one, then 150/100 daily days 2-5. Mild liver impairment: proceed. Severe liver impairment: not recommended.
Considerations for the 80yo case: Category X interaction - avoid combination of Paxlovid and Rivaroxaban. Ritonavir boosting can increase serum levels of Rivaroxaban, combination not recommended. Can consider Remdesivir instead, which does not have this interaction.

questions.model_answer:
a) Nirmatrelvir blocks the SARS-CoV-2 3C-like (main) protease, an enzyme required to cleave the viral polyproteins and permit replication; ritonavir is a CYP3A4 inhibitor given solely to slow nirmatrelvir metabolism so it remains at therapeutic concentrations.
b) Adults with moderate renal impairment, eGFR 30 to <60 mL/min: reduce to nirmatrelvir 150 mg with ritonavir 100 mg twice daily for 5 days (not recommended if eGFR <30 or Child-Pugh C cirrhosis).
c) (1) Contraindicated CYP3A interaction with rivaroxaban (bleeding risk, compounded by aspirin) - do not co-administer; other CYP3A-dependent drugs to check include amiodarone, colchicine, simvastatin/lovastatin, clozapine and triazolam. (2) Use remdesivir as the alternative outpatient antiviral if he remains within the treatment window and is high-risk. (3) Counsel on vaccination/booster once recovered, on warning symptoms prompting reassessment, and on possible viral/symptom rebound after therapy.
questions.beyond_mandell: Interaction list and renal cut-off follow the Paxlovid monograph and NIH COVID-19 treatment guidelines.

cohort_answer.text: Mechanism: Nirmatrelvir blocks the activity of the SARS-CoV-2-3CL protease, an enzyme required for viral replication; coadministration with ritonavir slows metabolism of nirmatrelvir so it remains active longer and at higher concentrations. Dose reduction population: eGFR 30-59 mL/min. Other considerations: CYP3A substrates - for medications highly dependent on CYP3A for clearance and potentially harmful at elevated levels, coadministration is contraindicated (includes alfuzosin, amiodarone, colchicine, clozapine, lurasidone, lovastatin, rivaroxaban, salmeterol, simvastatin, triazolam); if symptomatic can consider Remdesivir; COVID vaccine series and booster after recovery; counseling on warning symptoms and rebound

questions.question: Viral gastroenteritis: etiologic agents and their detection.

parts.text: Name 4 viral etiologies of gastroenteritis and 2 methods to detect them.

parts_raw.text: Name 4 viral etiologies of gastroenteritis and 2 methods to detect them.

questions.model_answer: Four viral etiologies: (1) Norovirus; (2) Rotavirus; (3) Enteric adenovirus (serotypes 40/41); (4) Astrovirus (Sapovirus also acceptable). Two detection methods: (1) Molecular assay - multiplex RT-PCR/PCR of stool (most sensitive, now first-line); (2) Antigen detection by enzyme immunoassay (EIA/ELISA) or lateral-flow immunochromatography on stool (widely used for rotavirus and enteric adenovirus). Electron microscopy of stool is an additional classic method.
questions.beyond_mandell: Not covered by the Rhinovirus chapter; based on Mandell chapters on viral gastroenteritis (Norovirus/Rotavirus/Astrovirus/enteric Adenovirus) and standard multiplex GI PCR/EIA diagnostics.

questions.question: COVID-19 (viruses).

parts.text: Name three proteins aside from the spike protein.
Name one approved treatment for mpox.
Describe remdesivir treatment efficacy as per animal models.

parts_raw.text: 3 proteins aside from Spike protein
1 approved treatment for Mpox
Remdesivir treatment efficacy as per animal models

questions.model_answer:
a) (1) Envelope (E). (2) Membrane (M). (3) Nucleocapsid (N).
b) Tecovirimat (TPOXX), an inhibitor of the orthopoxvirus VP37 envelope-wrapping protein required for formation and dissemination of infectious virions. (Brincidofovir/cidofovir are alternatives.)
c) In rhesus macaques inoculated with SARS-CoV-2 and treated with remdesivir 12 hours after inoculation, treated animals had no or markedly reduced respiratory disease (only 1 of 6 with dyspnea vs all untreated controls), lower lung viral loads and less severe lung pathology, though no reduction in upper respiratory shedding. Similar prophylactic and early-therapeutic benefit was shown in MERS-CoV macaque and mouse models and in Ebola virus-infected macaques.

cohort_answer.text:
3 proteins: Envelope; Membrane; Nucleocapsid.
Approved treatment for Mpox: Tecovirimat (Tpoxx) - potent inhibitor of an orthopoxvirus protein required for formation of an infectious virus particle, essential for dissemination within an infected host. (Cidofovir has in vitro activity against monkeypox virus and shown effective against lethal monkeypox virus challenge in animal models.)
Remdesivir efficacy in animal models: In a study of 12 macaques, 6 treated with Remdesivir and 6 not; of the 6 treated only 1 developed dyspnea vs all of the untreated. Outpatient treatment: 4/246 (1.6%) treated arm vs 21/252 (8.3%) placebo arm required a medical visit. Inpatient treatment: 1062 randomized to remdesivir or placebo; median recovery time 10 days vs 15 days; mortality at day 15: 6.7% vs 11.9%; mortality at day 29: 11.4% vs 15.2%.
